description: The place and the ground underfoot, read from the World IR by the host (PL.ground-from-ir, operator ruling U94(5)): the two inputs core's audio rules take and never look up. placeAt: settlement inside a geography.settlements[] circle, else wilderness (indoor is the host's own). groundSurfaceAt: an entities.roads[] road, then a closed, then an open geography.groundSurfaces[] surface, else the biome's open ground terrain.texture.ground, a default and never a refusal. footstepAt: the ground reading handed to footstepCue. IR metres on the ground plane {x, z}; y is never read. Runner: src/audio/ground-corpus.ts; every case is also re-run with the world's settlements, groundSurfaces and roads reversed and must agree. Regenerate with npm run audio-ground-corpus; npm run audio-ground-corpus:check fails on any difference.
sources: the reading characterised: unreal origin/main Source/InsimulRuntime/Portable/InsimulAudioPlace.{h,cpp} (P5.unreal.wired, unreal 214dc30), the host reading the P5 Unreal cell landed and asked about (run 7, p5 operator item 3).

core states it, and differs from that interim reading in four places, each pinned by a case here: the nearest shape or circle wins within a tier and then the smaller id (Unreal: the first listed); a ground surface with no archetype is read by its kind (Unreal: sidewalk for every kind); a road or open surface whose width is not positive, or a shape with a non-finite point, is not read; a position that is not finite has no reading.
the fixture is shaped like Unreal's ctest audio_place fixture (Brightwater's settlement circle of 31 m, a lane round the paved square, a footpath 2.4 m wide), with synthetic ids and names.
the IR fields: src/game-engine/ir-types.ts SettlementIR (position, radius), GroundSurfaceIR (id, kind, archetype, points, closed, width), RoadIR (fromId, toId, id, waypoints, width, archetype).
Every expected is core's answer; src/audio/__tests__/ground-from-ir.test.ts pins the same rules by hand.

contract.host: The host reads both facts from the World IR it holds and hands them to core's rules (ambientCues / AmbientSoundSystem / MusicInput take the place; footstepCue / stepFootsteps take the surface). Core's rules never read the IR for them.
contract.frame: IR world frame, metres, ground plane {x, z}; y (up) is never read. The host converts its listener position into this frame first (its own axes, units and level offset).
contract.noPosition: a point whose x or z is not a finite number has no reading (null); the host then hands footstepCue no surface, which steps as the default surface

place.field: geography.settlements[]: position {x, y, z} (the centre) and radius (metres)
place.rule: settlement when the plan distance to a centre is <= its radius; else wilderness. A settlement with no finite position or no positive finite radius is no circle. Overlaps: the nearest centre, then the smaller id. settlementName is name, else id.
place.indoor: never read from the IR: the host says when its listener is inside an interior

ground.road: entities.roads[]: within width/2 of the waypoints polyline (<=); surface archetype, else terrain.texture.road; id id, else road.<fromId>.<toId>
ground.closed: geography.groundSurfaces[] with closed true: inside the polygon its points enclose (even-odd)
ground.open: geography.groundSurfaces[] with closed not true: within width/2 of its points polyline (<=)
ground.within: within a tier the nearest shape wins (polyline distance; a closed surface is 0), then the smaller id
ground.notRead: a shape with any point that is not finite, or fewer than two points (a closed surface of two encloses nothing); a road or open surface whose width is not a positive finite number; settlements[].internalRoads and streetNetwork
ground.noGround: where no road or ground surface covers the point, including a world whose IR states none (or no geography, no entities, or is not an object): terrain.texture.ground, tier ground, shapeId null. A default, never a refusal; it steps as grass.

contract.later: sprint and crouch gaits: no host body reaches them yet (Village has walk only); a later feature, not this contract

cases.name: placeAt: 30 m from the centre of a 31 m circle is the settlement
placeAt: 32 m from it is the wilderness
placeAt: exactly on the radius is the settlement (distance <= radius)
placeAt: the height is never read (y 50 over the square is still the settlement)
placeAt: overlapping circles: the nearest centre wins, whatever the IR's order
placeAt: overlapping circles at an equal distance: the smaller id wins
placeAt: a settlement with no name answers its id as the name
placeAt: a settlement with radius 0, a negative radius or no position is no circle
placeAt: a world with no settlements is the wilderness everywhere
placeAt: a world with no geography is the wilderness everywhere
placeAt: a world that is not an object is the wilderness everywhere (never refused)
placeAt: a position that is not finite has no reading (null)
cases.note: The host has no position for the listener: it keeps its last place, or passes none. A string stands for NaN, which JSON cannot carry.

cases.name: placeAt: no position at all has no reading (null)
groundSurfaceAt: 1 m off the lane's centre line (half width 2.5 m) is the road, over the square it borders
cases.note: Roads are read before ground surfaces: the ground paint lays roads over plazas and footpaths.

cases.name: groundSurfaceAt: exactly half the width off the road is the road (<=)
groundSurfaceAt: 2.5 m off the road the other side, outside the square, is the road
groundSurfaceAt: 3 m off the road, outside the square, is the open ground
groundSurfaceAt: the middle of the square is the plaza
groundSurfaceAt: just outside the square is the open ground
groundSurfaceAt: 1.1 m off the footpath (half width 1.2 m) is the path
groundSurfaceAt: 1.3 m off it is the open ground
groundSurfaceAt: past the footpath's end, within its half width of the end point, is the path
groundSurfaceAt: the height is never read (y 40 over the square is still the plaza)
groundSurfaceAt: far from every shape is the open ground
groundSurfaceAt: NO GROUND STATED: a world with no ground surfaces and no roads is the open ground everywhere
cases.note: The default, never a refusal: the biome's own ground, terrain.texture.ground, with no shape.

cases.name: groundSurfaceAt: NO GROUND STATED: a world with no geography and no entities is the open ground
groundSurfaceAt: NO GROUND STATED: a world that is not an object is the open ground (never refused)
groundSurfaceAt: a settlement's internalRoads are not read
groundSurfaceAt: a road states its archetype: that is its surface
groundSurfaceAt: a road with a stated id answers that id
groundSurfaceAt: a plaza with no archetype is sidewalk
groundSurfaceAt: a footpath with no archetype is path
groundSurfaceAt: a ground surface of an unknown kind with no archetype is path
groundSurfaceAt: two roads: the nearer centre line wins, whatever the IR's order
groundSurfaceAt: two roads at an equal distance: the smaller id wins
groundSurfaceAt: two closed surfaces over one point: the smaller id wins
groundSurfaceAt: a closed surface is read before an open one over the same point
groundSurfaceAt: an open surface of width 0, a road of width 0, and a shape with a non-finite point are not read (the shape, not just the point)
groundSurfaceAt: a closed surface of two points encloses nothing
groundSurfaceAt: a position that is not finite has no reading (null)
footstepAt: walking on the road steps as stone
footstepAt: walking on the square steps as stone
footstepAt: walking on the footpath steps as grass (atelier has no dirt step)
footstepAt: running on the open ground steps as grass
footstepAt: NO GROUND STATED: a world with no ground surfaces or roads steps as grass, from the table (not the default)
cases.note: terrain.texture.ground has a row (grass). The stone default is only for a surface the host cannot name at all.

cases.name: footstepAt: NO POSITION: the host hands no surface, and the step is the default stone
footstepAt: a stated water surface underfoot makes no step
footstepAt: standing still on the road makes no step
